boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Thomas Jefferson University
boards.description: Ten currently documented food stops around Jefferson’s Center City campus, selected for later evening or overnight hours and under-21 access.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Chestnut
cards.subtitle: 1037 Chestnut St · Center City
cards.notes: Use the all-day-hours listing when an overnight food option is needed near the campus core; confirm your order method before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour, counter-service option on Chestnut Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official location page lists both dine-in and drive-thru service at 1037 Chestnut Street as open 24 hours every day.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists dine-in and drive-thru hours as open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Taco Bell at 1614 Chestnut
cards.subtitle: 1614 Chestnut St · Center City
cards.notes: Check the location page before heading west on Chestnut; its listed dine-in hours include service until midnight on Tuesday.
cards.short_summary: A Chestnut Street taco stop with midnight listed hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official page for 1614 Chestnut Street lists Tuesday dine-in hours from 10:00 AM to 12:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Tuesday dine-in service until 12:00 AM; verify other-day hours before visiting.

cards.title: Shake Shack Midtown Village
cards.subtitle: 105 S 12th St · 12th & Chestnut
cards.notes: Use the official order options for pickup or dine-in, and plan around the later Friday and Saturday closing time on the location page.
cards.short_summary: Burgers, chicken, hot dogs, and frozen custard near 12th Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Shake Shack lists its Midtown Village location at 105 South 12th Street and lists Friday and Saturday hours until 11:00 PM.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists dine-in, pickup, and delivery; Friday and Saturday close at 11:00 PM.

cards.title: Wendy’s Until 2 AM
cards.subtitle: 1515 Chestnut St · Center City
cards.notes: Keep this address handy for a later counter-service meal; the operator lists the same 2 AM restaurant closing time across the week.
cards.short_summary: A Chestnut Street Wendy’s with consistently late listed hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s official page for 1515 Chestnut Street lists restaurant hours of 6:30 AM–2:00 AM Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant hours until 2:00 AM every day.

cards.title: Bonchon in Chinatown
cards.subtitle: 1020 Cherry St · Chinatown
cards.notes: For a later sit-down or takeout meal, use the Cherry Street location page and note its 2 AM closing time on most listed days.
cards.short_summary: Korean fried chicken and Asian-fusion food with late listed hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Bonchon’s official page lists its Philadelphia restaurant at 1020 Cherry Street, open until 2:00 AM Monday through Saturday and until 11:00 PM Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours list 2:00 AM Monday–Saturday and 11:00 PM Sunday.

cards.title: Ishkabibble’s Original
cards.subtitle: 337 South St · South Street
cards.notes: Walk or arrange transport to the original South Street shop for a late sandwich stop; Friday and Saturday hours are listed through midnight.
cards.short_summary: The original Ishkabibble’s location with sandwiches and fries.
cards.evidence_claim: Ishkabibble’s official site identifies 337 South Street as the original location and lists Friday–Saturday hours from 9:30 AM to 12:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday–Saturday hours until 12:00 AM; Sunday–Thursday close at 11:00 PM.

cards.title: Ishkabibble’s II
cards.subtitle: 517 South St · South Street
cards.notes: Choose the second South Street location when you want the listed larger seating setup, and use the posted midnight weekend closing time.
cards.short_summary: A second Ishkabibble’s location with larger seating listed by the operator.
cards.evidence_claim: Ishkabibble’s official site identifies Ishkabibble’s II at 517 South Street as the location with large seating and lists Friday–Saturday hours until 12:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday–Saturday hours until 12:00 AM; Sunday–Thursday close at 11:00 PM.

cards.title: Masala Kitchen Rittenhouse
cards.subtitle: 2004 Chestnut St · Rittenhouse Square
cards.notes: For a Friday or Saturday evening meal, place an order before the stated last-call buffer and use the operator’s current location page for timing.
cards.short_summary: Indian food at a Chestnut Street location with midnight weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Masala Kitchen’s Rittenhouse location page lists Friday and Saturday hours until 12:00 AM and says final eat-in/takeout orders are taken 15 minutes before closing.
cards.access_notes: Friday and Saturday close at 12:00 AM; the operator says last eat-in/takeout orders are 15 minutes before closing.

cards.title: 15th St Pizza & Cheesesteak
cards.subtitle: 254 S 15th St · Center City
cards.notes: Use the counter’s daily 5 PM–3 AM window for slices, pies, or cheesesteaks, and confirm pickup timing if ordering a whole pie.
cards.short_summary: A Center City pizza-and-cheesesteak counter with daily 3 AM hours.
cards.evidence_claim: 15th St Pizza & Cheesesteak’s official site lists its address as 254 South 15th Street and states it is open daily from 5 PM until 3 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists daily hours of 5:00 PM–3:00 AM; whole pies require advance pickup ordering and are listed through midnight.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on Arch
cards.subtitle: 801 Arch St · near Chinatown
cards.notes: Use the official ordering page for carryout or delivery and rely on its listed 1 AM daily closing time when planning a later pizza order.
cards.short_summary: Pizza, wings, pasta, and desserts with daily 1 AM listed service.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut’s official page for 801 Arch Street lists delivery and carryout hours from 10:00 AM to 1:00 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists delivery and carryout hours until 1:00 AM daily.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented Jefferson study and gathering spaces across the Center City and East Falls campuses.

cards.title: Scott Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: Center City Campus · 1020 Walnut Street
cards.notes: Use the library as a starting point for an individual work session, then choose a quiet floor or reserve a room that fits your group.
cards.short_summary: A four-floor Center City library with study, learning, and collection-access spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson says Scott Memorial Library provides space and technology resources, with spaces and computers for study and learning across four floors.
cards.access_notes: Located on Jefferson’s Center City Campus; follow library and campus access requirements.

cards.entity_name: Scott Memorial Library Second-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Scott’s group study rooms
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City Campus
cards.notes: Reserve a second-floor room when your group needs a monitor, whiteboard, and power; arrive ready to end the session when the next booking begins.
cards.short_summary: Ten reservable group rooms equipped for shared academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: The library lists ten second-floor group study rooms for Jefferson students, with monitors, whiteboards, and power outlets.
cards.source_title: Scott Memorial Library | Student Study Spaces
cards.access_notes: Jefferson students only; reserve up to seven days ahead for up to four hours per day.

cards.entity_name: Scott Memorial Library Third-Floor Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: Scott’s individual study rooms
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City Campus
cards.notes: Book a third-floor room for focused solo work or a paired session, and collect the required key from Access Services before your reservation.
cards.short_summary: Six bookable individual rooms with desks, whiteboards, and power.
cards.evidence_claim: Scott Memorial Library has six third-floor individual study rooms equipped with whiteboards, desks, and power outlets.
cards.source_title: Scott Memorial Library | Student Study Spaces
cards.access_notes: Jefferson students only; reservations are limited to four hours daily and require a key from Access Services.

cards.entity_name: Scott Memorial Library Fourth-Floor Quiet Study
cards.title: Scott’s fourth-floor quiet study
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City Campus
cards.notes: Choose this floor when you need a quieter stretch of reading or review time; use the stairs while elevator service remains unavailable.
cards.short_summary: A reopened quiet-study floor at Scott Memorial Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson announced that Scott Memorial Library’s fourth floor is open for quiet study.
cards.source_title: 4th Floor Reopens at Scott Memorial Library
cards.access_notes: The published notice directs users to access the floor via stairs while elevator service is restored.

cards.title: Paul J. Gutman Library
cards.subtitle: East Falls Campus · 4201 Henry Avenue
cards.notes: Stop in for a quiet floor, group room, or librarian research help, and use the library’s East Falls location as a dependable study base.
cards.short_summary: The East Falls campus library offers quiet floors, group rooms, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson identifies Gutman Library as the East Falls campus library and directs visitors there for group study rooms, quiet floors, and librarian assistance.
cards.access_notes: Located on the East Falls Campus; consult the library’s reservation page for room eligibility.

cards.title: Gutman Study Room 101
cards.subtitle: Paul J. Gutman Library · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Reserve Room 101 for a larger project group when a shared display helps; make one four-hour booking and avoid consecutive room reservations.
cards.short_summary: A reservable 6–8 person study room with a plasma screen.
cards.evidence_claim: Gutman Library lists Study Room 101 as a 6–8 person reservable room with a plasma screen for computer projection.
cards.source_title: Paul J. Gutman Library | Reserving Space
cards.access_notes: Current students, faculty, and staff reserve with a Jefferson-issued email; one active four-hour reservation per patron.

cards.title: Rena Rowan Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Paul J. Gutman Library · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Book this room for a large-group study session when it is not needed for tutoring or instruction, and plan around its limited technology setup.
cards.short_summary: A bookable, up-to-20-person reading room that students may use for large-group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Gutman Library says students may book the Rena Rowan Reading Room for large-group study; it seats up to 20 people.
cards.source_title: Paul J. Gutman Library | Reserving Space
cards.access_notes: Primarily used for tutoring or instruction; students may book it for up to five hours. No technology or power outlets are listed.

cards.title: Kanbar Campus Center
cards.subtitle: East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Meet classmates in the shared seating areas or use the building’s student-facing services between classes; check the center’s posted schedule before going.
cards.short_summary: East Falls’ campus center combines meeting areas, dining, recreation, and Student Life offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson describes Kanbar Campus Center as an East Falls hub with meeting areas, a café/recreation area, dining, and Student Life offices.
cards.access_notes: Posted regular building hours are Monday–Friday 7:30 a.m.–midnight and weekends noon–midnight.

cards.entity_name: Jefferson Alumni Hall Northwest Student Lounge
cards.title: Northwest Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: Jefferson Alumni Hall · Center City Campus
cards.notes: Use the Northwest Student Lounge as an open student work break between classes, and leave enough time to exit before the listed closing time.
cards.short_summary: An open student lounge in Jefferson Alumni Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s study-space guide lists the Northwest Student Lounge in Jefferson Alumni Hall as open student space.
cards.access_notes: The guide lists this lounge as open 8 a.m.–11 p.m.; students using open study space must show Jefferson ID and may be asked to sign in.

cards.title: Curtis second-floor lobby
cards.subtitle: Curtis Building · Center City Campus
cards.notes: Set up in the second-floor lobby for an open study session, keeping your Jefferson ID available and following any security-desk sign-in instructions.
cards.short_summary: A designated open student space in the Curtis Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson designates the Curtis Building’s Second Floor Lobby as open student space.
cards.access_notes: The guide lists the lobby as open 8 a.m.–11 p.m.; students using open study space must show Jefferson ID and may be asked to sign in.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named Philadelphia places with direct evidence of free, no-purchase access.

cards.title: See the Liberty Bell
cards.subtitle: 6th and Market Streets, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Enter first-come, first-served, pass through screening, then move through the self-guided exhibits before seeing the bell.
cards.short_summary: A free, ticketless historic exhibit centered on the original Liberty Bell.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that admission is free and no tickets are required for the Liberty Bell Center.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; security screening is required and entry is first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Explore the President's House Site
cards.subtitle: 6th and Market Streets, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Walk the outdoor exhibit at your own pace and use its panels, videos, and visible foundations to discuss freedom and enslavement.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided outdoor exhibit interpreting the Washington household and enslaved people who lived there.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that the outdoor President's House Site is free and requires no tickets.
cards.source_title: Visiting the President's House Site: From Enslavement to Emancipation
cards.access_notes: Open daily, year-round, 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; outdoor exhibit entered from Market or 6th Street.

cards.title: Step into Old City Hall
cards.subtitle: 5th and Chestnut Streets, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Use the north Chestnut Street entrance and look into the restored Supreme Court chamber before continuing through the historic district.
cards.short_summary: A free first-come, first-served visit to an 18th-century Supreme Court chamber.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists free admission and no ticket requirement for Old City Hall's Supreme Court chamber.
cards.access_notes: The Supreme Court Chamber is open daily 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; entry is first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Browse the Merchants' Exchange exhibit
cards.subtitle: Walnut and 3rd Streets, Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Stop into the lobby exhibit to examine the building's role in Philadelphia's nineteenth-century financial and postal history.
cards.short_summary: A free lobby exhibit inside a landmark designed by William Strickland.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists the Merchants' Exchange Building lobby exhibit as free and ticketless.
cards.access_notes: Lobby exhibit is open Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; the building is wheelchair accessible.

cards.title: Watch printing at Franklin Court
cards.subtitle: Franklin Court, between 3rd and 4th Streets
cards.notes: Visit the public viewing area to see the eighteenth-century-style printing operation, then explore the surrounding Franklin Court passageway.
cards.short_summary: A free historic printing stop within Independence National Historical Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies the Franklin Court Printing Office among sites requiring no tickets and no fee.
cards.access_notes: Confirm daily building operations before going; the NPS identifies a designated public viewing area in the Printing Office.

cards.title: Meet at the LOVE Sculpture
cards.subtitle: LOVE Park, 16th Street and JFK Boulevard
cards.notes: Use the surrounding walking paths and seating for a photo stop or an easy meetup before heading along the Benjamin Franklin Parkway.
cards.short_summary: A public-art gathering point in John F. Kennedy Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Philadelphia identifies the LOVE Sculpture as free to visit at LOVE Park.
cards.source_title: 40+ Free Things to Do in Greater Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: The sculpture is in the outdoor public space of LOVE Park; park amenities and nearby vendors may charge separately.

cards.title: Use Dilworth Park's public space
cards.subtitle: 1 S. 15th Street, beside Philadelphia City Hall
cards.notes: Bring a friend to sit under the tree groves, walk through the plaza, or check the calendar for a free lawn screening or performance.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor City Hall plaza with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Philadelphia states that there is no cost of admission to visit Dilworth Park.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space; skating, food, and other programmed amenities can have separate charges.

cards.title: Walk The Rail Park
cards.subtitle: 1300 Noble Street entrance; also Callowhill Street between 11th and 12th
cards.notes: Enter at Noble Street for the accessible slope, then take a slow loop past benches, plantings, industrial artwork, and the Story Wall.
cards.short_summary: A free elevated park built on former Reading Railroad tracks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rail Park's official site states that Phase One is free and open daily.
cards.access_notes: Phase One is free and open daily; use the Noble Street entrance for wheelchair-accessible access.

cards.title: Lounge at Spruce Street Harbor Park
cards.subtitle: Penn's Landing waterfront
cards.notes: Use the seating, lights, floating gardens, and hammocks for a waterfront meetup; skip the optional concessions and paid activities.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal public waterfront park with free entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Philadelphia states that Spruce Street Harbor Park is free and open to the public through September, with concessions and select activities separate.
cards.source_title: Spruce Street Harbor Park: 5 New & Surprising Things to Do for 2026
cards.access_notes: Seasonal and free through September; concessions and select activities are pay-as-you-go.

cards.title: Climb the Rocky Steps
cards.subtitle: Philadelphia Museum of Art, 2600 Benjamin Franklin Parkway
cards.notes: Take the outdoor staircase at your own pace, pause at the top for the skyline view, and keep the visit outside the museum's ticketed galleries.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor stair climb and skyline-view stop at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Philadelphia identifies the Rocky Steps as free and says visitors can run the steps or visit the Rocky Statue without museum admission.
cards.source_title: 40+ Free Things to Do in Greater Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: This card covers the exterior steps only; entry to the Philadelphia Museum of Art galleries is separate.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Jefferson library study environments across the Center City and East Falls campuses, with access and setup details verified from current university library pages.

cards.title: Scott Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City
cards.notes: Settle into the first-floor Reading Room for a library-based work session; bring your Jefferson ID and follow building access procedures.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor reading environment in Scott Memorial Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s study-space guide identifies a Reading Room on the first floor of Scott Memorial Library.
cards.access_notes: Center City open study-space users must show a Jefferson ID and may be asked to sign in and out at Security.

cards.title: Scott’s Collaboration Rooms
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City
cards.notes: Reserve or use a second-floor group room when working with classmates; the rooms provide a computer, monitor, writing surface, and connection cables.
cards.short_summary: Small-group rooms equipped for shared screen work and whiteboard planning.
cards.evidence_claim: Scott Memorial Library has ten second-floor small-group collaboration rooms with computers, large monitors, writing surfaces, and laptop/iPad cables.
cards.access_notes: Six west-side rooms are unlocked 8am–2am; four east-side rooms may be reserved. Jefferson ID requirements apply.

cards.title: Scott’s Casual Reading Area
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City
cards.notes: Use the named second-floor Casual Reading Area when you want an informal library setting; keep personal items with you and clear your workspace afterward.
cards.short_summary: An identified casual study setting on Scott Library’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s study-space guide identifies a Casual Reading Area on the second floor of Scott Memorial Library.
cards.access_notes: Center City open study-space users must show a Jefferson ID and may be asked to sign in and out at Security.

cards.title: Scott’s Group Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City
cards.notes: Meet at the second-floor group tables for a collaborative session without booking a room; use the library’s nearby group-study area responsibly.
cards.short_summary: Named tables in Scott Library’s second-floor group-study zone.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s study-space guide identifies Group Study Tables on the second floor of Scott Memorial Library.
cards.access_notes: The second floor includes group options including carrels, tables, and study rooms; Jefferson ID requirements apply.

cards.title: Scott Third-Floor Carrels
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City
cards.notes: Choose a third-floor carrel for quiet individual work; this floor is designated for quiet study and has carrels, pods, and tables.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-floor carrel option for focused library work.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of Scott Memorial Library provides carrels, pods, and tables for quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Quiet study is on Scott’s third and fourth floors; Center City open-space users must show Jefferson ID.

cards.title: Scott Fourth-Floor Carrels
cards.subtitle: Scott Memorial Library · Center City
cards.notes: Head to the fourth-floor carrels when your work calls for a quiet setup; observe the floor’s quiet-study designation while you are there.
cards.short_summary: A separate quiet-floor carrel setting in Scott Memorial Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s study-space guide identifies Study Carrels on the fourth floor and says the fourth floor provides quiet-study carrels, pods, and tables.
cards.access_notes: Quiet study is on Scott’s third and fourth floors; Center City open-space users must show Jefferson ID.

cards.title: Gutman Room 101
cards.subtitle: Paul J. Gutman Library · East Falls
cards.notes: Book Room 101 for a larger project meeting or presentation practice; it seats six to eight and includes a plasma screen for computer projection.
cards.short_summary: A reservable, larger-capacity group room with projection.
cards.evidence_claim: Gutman Library’s Study Room 101 seats six to eight people, includes a plasma screen for computer projection, and can be reserved by Jefferson students.
cards.source_title: Paul J. Gutman Library | Reserving Space
cards.access_notes: Current students, faculty, and staff reserve with a Jefferson-issued email; one reservation at a time for a four-hour window.

cards.title: Gutman’s Quiet-Zone Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Paul J. Gutman Library · East Falls
cards.notes: Reserve a second-floor study room for a small group that needs lower-noise surroundings; each room seats three to four people in the quiet zone.
cards.short_summary: Reservable small-group rooms inside Gutman’s quiet zone.
cards.evidence_claim: Gutman Library says its first- and second-floor study rooms seat three to four people and that the second-floor spaces are in a quiet zone.
cards.source_title: Paul J. Gutman Library | Reserving Space
cards.access_notes: Available to current Jefferson students, faculty, and staff through the self-service booking system for a four-hour window.

cards.title: Rena Rowan Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Paul J. Gutman Library · East Falls
cards.notes: Reserve the Rena Rowan Reading Room when a larger study group needs room to spread out; it seats up to 20 and can be booked for up to five hours.
cards.short_summary: A large-group reading room available for student study bookings.
cards.evidence_claim: Gutman Library states that students may book the Rena Rowan Reading Room for large group study; it seats up to 20 and is available up to five hours.
cards.source_title: Paul J. Gutman Library | Reserving Space
cards.access_notes: Primarily intended for faculty- or staff-led tutoring or instruction, but students may book it for large-group study.

cards.title: Gutman Ground-Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: Paul J. Gutman Library · East Falls
cards.notes: Use Gutman’s ground-floor quiet-study area for individual work, choosing from the available quiet space and individual carrels across that floor.
cards.short_summary: Ground-floor quiet space with individual study carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson identifies quiet study space throughout Gutman Library’s ground floor, including individual study carrels.
cards.access_notes: Gutman’s posted schedule is Monday–Thursday 8am–2am, Friday 8am–9pm, Saturday 10am–5pm, and Sunday noon–2am.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten Center City corridors near Jefferson’s Philadelphia campus, each anchored by a named, publicly documented destination.

cards.title: Arch Street: Reading Terminal Market
cards.subtitle: Arch Street corridor — Reading Terminal Market at 12th Street
cards.notes: Enter from Arch Street and use the market’s official directory to choose one vendor or browse the public-market aisles before heading back to campus.
cards.short_summary: A historic indoor public market with more than 80 merchants.
cards.evidence_claim: Reading Terminal Market is at 51 N. 12th Street and has more than 80 merchants.
cards.source_title: Reading Terminal Market: America's Best Public Market
cards.access_notes: Check the market’s official website for current vendor and building hours.

cards.title: Arch Street: Pennsylvania Convention Center
cards.subtitle: Arch Street corridor — Pennsylvania Convention Center at 11th Street
cards.notes: Walk the Arch Street frontage to see the convention center’s scale, then check its official calendar before planning around a public event.
cards.short_summary: A six-block convention complex with an Arch Street entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pennsylvania Convention Center is at 1101 Arch Street; its Arch Street entrance leads toward Reading Terminal Market and the historic district.
cards.access_notes: Public access depends on scheduled events; consult the center’s official calendar and event policies.

cards.title: Market Street: Fashion District Philadelphia
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — Fashion District at 9th Street
cards.notes: Use the Market Street entrance, then consult the official directory for current shops, food counters, entertainment, and accessibility details.
cards.short_summary: A three-block indoor retail and entertainment destination on East Market.
cards.evidence_claim: Fashion District Philadelphia is at 901 Market Street and spans three city blocks along East Market Street.
cards.access_notes: Official visitor information lists variable hours; verify current hours before going.

cards.title: North Broad Street: Masonic Temple
cards.subtitle: North Broad Street corridor — Masonic Temple at City Hall
cards.notes: Photograph the landmark exterior from Broad Street, or reserve a guided tour through the official site to see its historic interiors.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark housing the Masonic Library and Museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Masonic Temple at One North Broad Street is a National Historic Landmark and home to the Masonic Library and Museum.
cards.access_notes: Guided tours and admission are offered through the official site; availability may vary.

cards.title: South 15th Street: Dilworth Park
cards.subtitle: South 15th Street corridor — Dilworth Park beside City Hall
cards.notes: Use the seating and pedestrian space as a pause point, then check the official park calendar for seasonal performances or recreation programming.
cards.short_summary: A City Hall public space with a programmable fountain and seasonal uses.
cards.evidence_claim: Dilworth Park is at 1 S. 15th Street and includes a programmable fountain, lawns, seating, and seasonal programming.
cards.access_notes: The park is outdoors; seasonal activities and event access vary. Check the official calendar.

cards.entity_name: LOVE Park / John F. Kennedy Plaza
cards.title: JFK Boulevard: LOVE Park
cards.subtitle: John F. Kennedy Boulevard corridor — LOVE Park at 15th Street
cards.notes: Stop at the LOVE sculpture on the park’s east side, then use the City’s park information to confirm any current public programming.
cards.short_summary: A civic plaza documented by the City as the site of the LOVE sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies LOVE Park / John F. Kennedy Plaza at 1501 John F. Kennedy Boulevard and places the LOVE sculpture on its eastern side.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public park; organized activities may require reservations or permits.

cards.title: Arch Street: African American Museum
cards.subtitle: Arch Street corridor — African American Museum in Philadelphia at 7th Street
cards.notes: Use the museum’s current exhibition listings to plan a visit, and pause outside to view the documented public sculptures at the building.
cards.short_summary: A museum interpreting African American history and culture in Philadelphia.
cards.evidence_claim: The African American Museum in Philadelphia is at 701 Arch Street and was founded in 1976 to preserve, interpret, and exhibit African American heritage and culture.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and exhibition access are subject to its current visitor policies.

cards.title: Arch Street: National Constitution Center
cards.subtitle: Arch Street corridor — National Constitution Center at 5th Street
cards.notes: Plan around the museum’s official daily schedule and pick an exhibit or live program before walking east through Independence National Historical Park.
cards.short_summary: A museum and civic education center focused on the U.S. Constitution.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Constitution Center is an interactive museum, national town hall, and civic education headquarters at 525 Arch Street.
cards.access_notes: Official visitor information lists daily museum hours; admission is ticketed.

cards.title: South 22nd Street: Mütter Museum
cards.subtitle: South 22nd Street corridor — Mütter Museum near Market Street
cards.notes: Review the museum’s current exhibition guidance before visiting, especially if medical-history collections may not suit everyone in your group.
cards.short_summary: A medical-history museum with collections of anatomical and pathological materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mütter Museum is at 19 S. 22nd Street and its collection includes bones, plaster casts, medical illustrations, and pathological specimens.
cards.access_notes: Admission and visitor guidance are set by the museum; review its official website before going.

cards.title: North 6th Street: Franklin Square
cards.subtitle: North 6th Street corridor — Franklin Square at Race Street
cards.notes: Walk the square’s paths and fountain area, then check the official operator’s calendar for any seasonal light show or family programming.
cards.short_summary: A public square with a historic fountain, green space, and seasonal attractions.
cards.evidence_claim: Franklin Square is at 200 N. 6th Street and includes green space, a carousel, playgrounds, and the Franklin Square Fountain.
cards.source_title: Your Guide to the 25 Best Parks in Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: The outdoor square is publicly accessible; individual attractions and seasonal programming may charge admission.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Jefferson rituals spanning arrival, professional milestones, design, music, and medical-school celebration.

cards.title: Enter Convocation Through a Faculty Welcome Line
cards.subtitle: Incoming-class Convocation, East Falls
cards.notes: At Convocation, follow the incoming class along the walkway into the Gallagher Center while university leaders, faculty, and staff cheer.
cards.short_summary: A public, cheering welcome marks the start of the undergraduate journey.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson describes leaders, faculty, and staff cheering as incoming students and families stream down the walkway into Gallagher Center as an annual Convocation tradition.
cards.access_notes: Part of incoming-student Convocation programming; attendance and guest details vary by year.

cards.title: Nominate a Teacher Who Got You Here
cards.subtitle: Incoming-class Convocation, East Falls
cards.notes: Before Convocation, think of an educator who shaped your path and submit a nomination when the incoming-class process opens.
cards.short_summary: New Jefferson students formally recognize a pre-college educator.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson identifies incoming students nominating a remarkable educator who influenced their academic lives as a special Convocation tradition.
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to Convocation and may be limited to the incoming class.

cards.entity_name: Sidney Kimmel Medical College White Coat Ceremony
cards.title: Receive the First White Coat
cards.subtitle: Sidney Kimmel Medical College
cards.notes: Join the entering medical class and invited supporters for the white-coat presentation that formally begins the Jefferson medical-school journey.
cards.short_summary: A white-coat presentation welcomes each new SKMC class to medicine.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson says the White Coat Ceremony marks the official start of the Sidney Kimmel Medical College Class of 2027's medical-school journey.
cards.source_title: On a Path With Purpose, Med Students Receive Their White Coats
cards.access_notes: For SKMC entering students; ceremony timing, venue, and guest arrangements are announced by the college.

cards.title: Recite the Hippocratic Oath in the New Coat
cards.subtitle: Sidney Kimmel Medical College White Coat Ceremony
cards.notes: During the White Coat Ceremony, take part in the class oath recital that connects the first coat with patient-focused professional commitments.
cards.short_summary: Jefferson's new medical students pair the first coat with an oath recital.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson reports that SKMC students recited the Maimonides Prayer for the Physician and the Hippocratic Oath as part of the White Coat Ceremony.
cards.source_title: On a Path With Purpose, Med Students Receive Their White Coats
cards.access_notes: For White Coat Ceremony participants; the exact program may change by class year.

cards.entity_name: Jefferson College of Pharmacy White Coat Ceremony
cards.title: Be Coated by a Pharmacy Faculty Advisor
cards.subtitle: Jefferson College of Pharmacy
cards.notes: Attend the pharmacy class ceremony, where each student receives a white coat from a faculty advisor to begin the professional journey.
cards.short_summary: Student pharmacists receive their first professional coat from faculty.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson says each Jefferson College of Pharmacy student received a white coat from a faculty advisor during the 2023 ceremony.
cards.access_notes: For entering Jefferson College of Pharmacy students; check college communications for current details.

cards.title: Close the Pharmacy Coat Ceremony With the Oath
cards.subtitle: Jefferson College of Pharmacy
cards.notes: At the pharmacy white-coat ceremony, join the class in reciting the Oath of a Pharmacist after the individual coat presentations.
cards.short_summary: The incoming pharmacy class voices its professional oath together.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson states that its 2023 Jefferson College of Pharmacy White Coat Ceremony concluded with students reciting the Oath of the Pharmacist.
cards.access_notes: For participants in the pharmacy White Coat Ceremony; confirm the current ceremony program with the college.

cards.title: Return Each Spring for the Student Fashion Show
cards.subtitle: College of Fashion & Textiles
cards.notes: Follow the annual spring show to see Jefferson fashion-design work presented as a celebration of students’ four-year creative development.
cards.short_summary: Each spring, Jefferson stages a student fashion-design celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson says each spring brings its Annual Student Fashion Design Show, celebrating Fashion Design students' work.
cards.source_title: Fashion & Textile Design Courses & Degree Programs
cards.access_notes: Scheduled in spring; public access, tickets, and venue details vary by edition.

cards.title: Send Senior Collections Down Jefferson’s Runway
cards.subtitle: Annual Fashion Show, College of Fashion & Textiles
cards.notes: For a senior capstone milestone, prepare a collection for the annual show’s runway presentation and its audience of peers and industry guests.
cards.short_summary: Fashion Design seniors are invited to present capstone collections on the runway.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson says every Fashion Design senior is invited to showcase a capstone collection on the runway at the Annual Fashion Show.
cards.access_notes: For Fashion Design seniors; show production and audience details are set for each annual event.

cards.title: Keep a Piece of Handel’s Messiah in the Concert
cards.subtitle: Thomas Jefferson University Choir
cards.notes: Listen for the Jefferson University Choir’s recurring Handel selection in its concert repertoire, alongside classical, rock, jazz, and newer works.
cards.short_summary: A portion of Handel’s Messiah is a recurring University Choir tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson Magazine identifies part of Handel's Messiah as an annual tradition for the Thomas Jefferson University Choir.
cards.access_notes: Concert dates and repertoire are announced by the choir; performance access varies by event.

cards.title: Open the Residency Envelope Together at Noon
cards.subtitle: Sidney Kimmel Medical College Match Day
cards.notes: At Match Day, gather with the graduating medical class and loved ones for the coordinated envelope opening that reveals residency placements.
cards.short_summary: Jefferson medical students share the residency reveal with classmates and supporters.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson reports that the SKMC Class of 2026 tore open envelopes at Match Day to learn where they would complete residencies.
cards.source_title: Match Day Marks Defining Moment for Jefferson Medical Students
cards.access_notes: For eligible fourth-year SKMC students; event attendance and supporter arrangements are set by the college.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Thomas Jefferson University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key East Falls sequence for learning the campus, getting set up, and sampling its academic, social, and recreation spaces.

cards.title: Start by getting your campus bearings
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Stop at the Kanbar information desk to handle your photo ID, then use the meeting areas to make a simple weekend plan with your map open.
cards.short_summary: The campus social hub and a practical first stop for ID setup.
cards.evidence_claim: Kanbar Campus Center houses the information desk and provides meeting areas, dining, a bookstore, Student Life offices, and recreation space.
cards.access_notes: Regular building hours are posted by Jefferson; photo IDs are issued at the information desk during those hours.

cards.title: Have a first campus meal
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Choose a dinner station that suits your needs, note the dining setup, and keep the meal simple while you learn where campus services are.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus dining hall with weekday brunch, dinner, and weekend brunch service.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson describes Ravenhill as offering retail weekday brunch and all-you-care-to-eat dining for dinner and weekend brunch.
cards.access_notes: Consult Jefferson Dining Services for current meal periods and payment options.

cards.title: Take a quiet Ravenhill pause
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Ravenhill Campus
cards.notes: Walk over to the chapel exterior and nearby breezeway for a calm reset; respect residential areas and follow any posted building-access rules.
cards.short_summary: A named Ravenhill landmark connected to the Mott Hall and Mansion area.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson identifies Ravenhill Chapel as connected with Mott Hall and Ravenhill Mansion through a shared breezeway.
cards.access_notes: Use exterior and common areas only as permitted; Mott Hall is a residence hall.

cards.title: Locate your research home base
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Find the library on the campus map, check its current service information, and identify one place to return for research or course materials.
cards.short_summary: East Falls’ named university library and a useful academic anchor.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s East Falls campus map lists Paul J. Gutman Library as a campus destination.
cards.source_title: Thomas Jefferson University East Falls Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Check library access and service hours before planning a study visit.

cards.title: See where design work takes shape
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · Lubert Plaza
cards.notes: Walk to the Architecture & Design Center, take in the building from the plaza, and use Jefferson’s tour material to understand its academic role.
cards.short_summary: A former library now used by Jefferson’s architecture and design programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson states that the Architecture & Design Center, built in 1967, was transformed from the university’s first library into the College of Architecture, Design & Engineering’s home.
cards.access_notes: View from public campus areas and follow building-access rules.

cards.title: Add the Art Center to your map
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Make the Art Center one landmark on your campus loop, photograph the exterior if permitted, and check posted information before entering any studio areas.
cards.short_summary: A named East Falls academic building suited to a visual campus-orientation stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s East Falls emergency-preparedness page lists the Art Center among campus buildings.
cards.access_notes: Observe posted access requirements; studio and classroom access may be limited.

cards.entity_name: Gallagher Athletic, Recreation and Convocation Center
cards.title: Find your movement option
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Locate the Gallagher Center and check the current recreation schedule; bring your Jefferson ID if you plan to use facilities that require card access.
cards.short_summary: A campus athletics and recreation center with courts, fitness space, and a jogging track.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson describes the Gallagher Center as containing basketball courts, a fitness center, aerobics studio, racquetball court, and elevated jogging track.
cards.access_notes: Jefferson states that a photo ID provides access to the Gallagher Athletic Center; verify current recreation policies before visiting.

cards.title: Walk past a campus field
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Use Alumni Field as an outdoor waypoint while learning the north side of campus, and keep clear of practices, games, and any marked restricted areas.
cards.short_summary: A named athletic-field destination on Jefferson’s East Falls map.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s East Falls campus map identifies Alumni Field as a campus destination.
cards.source_title: Thomas Jefferson University East Falls Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Field availability depends on scheduled athletics and campus operations.

cards.title: Spot a historic Ravenhill landmark
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Ravenhill Campus
cards.notes: Include the mansion exterior on your walking loop, then follow the paths back toward residence areas without entering spaces reserved for residents or events.
cards.short_summary: A named Ravenhill landmark beside the chapel and Mott Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson identifies Ravenhill Mansion as part of the Ravenhill Campus area connected to Mott Hall and Ravenhill Chapel.
cards.access_notes: Enjoy from public exterior areas unless an authorized campus event provides access.

cards.entity_name: Center for Sustainability, Energy Efficiency and Design (SEED Center)
cards.title: Finish with a campus-map check-in
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · East Falls Campus
cards.notes: Use the SEED Center as your final map landmark, then review the route you walked and save the interactive campus map for your first week.
cards.short_summary: A named East Falls destination focused on sustainability, energy efficiency, and design.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson’s East Falls campus map lists the Center for Sustainability, Energy Efficiency and Design (SEED Center).
cards.source_title: Thomas Jefferson University East Falls Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Follow posted building-access requirements; use the official interactive map for current navigation.
